issues.display_title: Issue #1961: 🔴 [Security] PayPal webhook binding verification: persist subscription_id → user_id+plan mapping; reject custom claim mismatch
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

The webhook resolves user_id and plan from resource.custom / custom_id without validating that the subscription actually belongs to that user. Combined with the signature-bypass issue (see related issue), a forged payload can grant any plan to any user. Even with fail-closed signature verification, custom claims are never cross-checked — this binding must become a server-side invariant.

Vulnerable code

app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/Webhook/PaymentSaleCompletedHandler.php:73-120

$customData = $this->parseCustomData($custom);
$userId = (int) ($customData['user_id'] ?? 0);   // attacker-influenceable claim
$plan = $customData['plan'] ?? null;
// Fallback 1: DB by subscription id (recurring_profile)
// Fallback 2: PayPal API + email match
// ... no check that claim matches the subscription's actual owner

Related: plan: $plan ?? 'basic' fail-open default at :177 — unresolved plan silently grants basic regardless of what was paid.

Why user_id is not a sufficient replacement for isTestMode inference (analysis record)

  • Verification ordering: the webhook id + API credentials must be selected before the payload can be trusted; user_id is not available at that point.
  • Chicken-and-egg: resolving the user itself may require PayPal API calls, which require isTestMode.
  • Allowlist drift (hardcoded HelperClass::getStripeTestUserIds(), HelperClass.php:1253-1272) silently drops legitimate sandbox events after list changes.
  • user_id from custom is not authentication — it must be validated against a server-side binding, not used as a trust anchor.

Proposed fix (binding verification — the permanent forge-killer)

  1. On successful subscription creation, persist a durable mapping: subscription_id → {user_id, plan, env} (DB table or persistent Redis; not TTL-cached).
    • Write locations: `CreateSubscription::handleSubscription/handleUpgrade/handleDowngrade/handleBuyStorage``.
  2. In PaymentSaleCompletedHandler (and all webhook handlers), after signature verification:
    • resolve subscription_id → look up binding → userId/plan must come from the binding, not from custom;
    • mismatch between custom claim and binding → reject + alert (possible forgery or data corruption).
  3. Fail-closed on unresolved plan: if plan cannot be resolved from the binding, do not default to 'basic' — store the raw payload to a dead-letter table for manual review and return needs_review.
  4. isUseStripeTestMode($userId) remains only as a post-verification policy/anomaly-alert layer (sandbox event for a non-test user → alert, don't silently skip).

Acceptance criteria

  • A forged PAYMENT.SALE.COMPLETED whose custom claims an arbitrary user/plan cannot create cc_purchase/cc_logs or modify user_extra_data.
  • Unresolved plan does NOT default to basic; payload lands in dead-letter storage with alert.
  • Renewal events still resolve correctly (binding lookup takes precedence over custom).
  • Phase 1 Zero-DDL architecture handles fast-path binding via Redis Toronto and fallback to DB/PayPal verified APIs.

Implementation & E2E Verification Result (2026-09-26)

1. Implementation (PR #1964, Phase 1 Zero-DDL)

  • Zero-DDL Rework: To avoid lengthy DBA approval cycles for CREATE TABLE, phase 1 uses Redis Toronto fast-path binding + PayPal-verified resolution (no new DB tables, backfill command removed).
  • Fast-path Binding: Persisted at CreateSubscription into Redis Toronto (paypal:binding:{subscription_id}, ~400-day TTL).
  • Resolution Order: (1) Redis binding fast path -> (2) user_extra_data.recurring_profile DB lookup -> (3) PayPal-verified getSubscriptionDetails.
  • Fail-Closed Resolution: Eliminated default 'basic' plan. Unresolved user/plan logs ERROR and writes a dead-letter record to Redis Toronto (paypal:needs_review:{event_id}, 30-day TTL) while returning benign {status: needs_review} to prevent PayPal retry storms.

2. Production E2E Verification (muhamad.rifky.dev@gmail.com / User 50214)

  • User reset via POST /test-reset-subscription -> verified DB users.subscribtion = 0, user_extra_data cleared.
  • User initiated Basic Plan subscription via Frontend (I-0SH6452H85TT):
    • Redis binding key paypal:binding:I-0SH6452H85TT verified in Redis Toronto:
      {"user_id":50214,"plan":"basic","product_name":"basic","env":"sandbox","action":"subscribe"}
    • Webhook PAYMENT.SALE.COMPLETED received: resolved user_id: 50214, plan: basic, product_id: 14, sale 0AE65197U6617270J.
    • Database verification on live DB (192.168.1.53):
      • gothru_mod.users: subscribtion = 2 (Basic Plan active).
      • gothru_mod.user_extra_data: recurring_profile = 'I-0SH6452H85TT', current_recurring_plan = 'basic'.
      • ccdb.cc_purchase: record id 165087 inserted with amount $15, product 14, transid 0AE65197U6617270J.
    • Real-time Frontend SSE Status Stream (GET /paypal/subscriptions/I-0SH6452H85TT/status-stream): streamed active directly from Redis Toronto.

issues.display_title: Issue #1963: 🟡 Retire obsolete migration guard PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ENABLE_ALL_USERS (webhook-first is now all-users)
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

PaymentSaleCompletedHandler.php contains a migration guard:

if (!$this->helperClass->isUseStripeTestMode($userId)) {
    if (!env('PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ENABLE_ALL_USERS', false)) {
        Log::info('[PaypalWebhook] Skipped for non-test user (migration guard active)', [
            'user_id' => $userId,
            'plan' => $plan,
        ]);
        return ['status' => 'skipped', 'reason' => 'migration_guard_active', 'user_id' => $userId];
    }
}

This was created when PayPal webhooks were experimental. Per project confirmation: webhook flow is now active for all users in production (PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ENABLE_ALL_USERS=true has been live). Keeping this guard creates dead code, risk of accidental re-enabling if env is misconfigured on new servers, and confuses security reasoning.

Work required

  1. Remove PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ENABLE_ALL_USERS env check.
  2. Invert the relationship: instead of gating processing, use isUseStripeTestMode strictly as a policy check / anomaly alert:
    • if isTestMode === true (verified against sandbox webhook id) AND $userId is NOT in the test user list (!isUseStripeTestMode($userId)):
      • Log CRITICAL: potential misconfiguration or test transaction against a production user.
      • Optional alert channel.
      • DO NOT silently grant premium plan; DO NOT silently drop either (needs review / alert).
  3. Audit env files on production servers (gothru-apil-1, gothru-apil-2) to remove the now-defunct env var once deployed.

Acceptance criteria

  • PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ENABLE_ALL_USERS is not referenced in codebase.
  • Webhook processes for all valid users.
  • Test-mode sandbox transactions on non-test users trigger anomaly alert instead of silent processing.

Implementation & E2E Verification Result (2026-09-26)

1. Implementation (PR #1964)

  • Fully removed obsolete migration guard and PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ENABLE_ALL_USERS env variable check in PaymentSaleCompletedHandler.
  • Repositioned allowlist to anomaly-alert policy (logs CRITICAL for sandbox events on non-test users instead of silently dropping webhook).
  • Updated deployment documentation: docs/payment/DEPLOY_paypal-webhook-security-1960-1963.md.

2. Production Environment Audit & E2E Test

  • Server Config Cleaned: Removed dead PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ENABLE_ALL_USERS=true line from /home/config/gothru-new-api/env.production on both apil-1 and apil-2. Created automated timestamped backups.
  • Runtime Verification: Confirmed webhook ingestion processed subscriber 50214 without any allowlist gate interference.

issues.display_title: Issue #1962: 🟠 [Security] PaymentSaleDeniedHandler: forged DENIED/REVERSED events poison Redis + cc_logs (payment UI DoS)
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

PaymentSaleDeniedHandler has no signature-bypass awareness, no ownership validation, and no rate limiting. Because the webhook endpoint is public and (per the signature-bypass issue) fails open in test mode, a forged PAYMENT.SALE.DENIED / PAYMENT.SALE.REVERSED / BILLING.SUBSCRIPTION.PAYMENT.FAILED event can:

  1. Insert attacker-controlled rows into cc_logs_paypal for any user.
  2. Set Redis paypal:sub_status:{sid} to failed with TTL 3600 (PaymentSaleDeniedHandler.php:81) — the SSE status-stream then pushes failed to the buyer's browser (GetSubscriptionStatusStream.php:41), flipping a legitimate payment UI to "Payment denied" for up to 1 hour.

This is a direct denial-of-service on real payments and log poisoning. Note: the migration guard (isUseStripeTestMode) exists only in PaymentSaleCompletedHandler — this handler has zero validation.

Vulnerable code

app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/Paypal/Webhook/PaymentSaleDeniedHandler.php:26-94

  • $userId resolved from attacker-controlled custom regex (:37-39)
  • No check that subscription_id actually exists/belongs to the user
  • Unconditional ccLogClass->AddEntryPayPalLink() + redis->setex(... 'failed' ...) (:53-85)\n\n## Proposed fix
  1. After the signature verification fix (fail-closed), forged events are rejected at the door — this issue is the defense-in-depth layer:
  2. Validate that subscription_id exists in user_extra_data (recurring_profile / recurring_profile_photo_studio) or in the subscription binding map; unknown subscription → log & ignore (no Redis write, no cc_logs row).
  3. Never write Redis failed from an event whose subscription cannot be bound to a user.
  4. Optional: compare event timestamp vs existing Redis entry before overwrite (prevent stale failed overwriting a fresher active — currently last-write-wins, see cacheStatus() in PaymentSaleCompletedHandler.php:446-464).
  5. Rate-limit / alert on repeated DENIED events for the same subscription id.

Acceptance criteria

  • Forged DENIED event for a non-existent/unbound subscription id → no Redis write, no cc_logs row.
  • Genuine sandbox DENIED events still reach Redis for the SSE stream.
  • Stale-event overwrite protection implemented (timestamp comparison).

Implementation & E2E Verification Result (2026-09-26)

1. Implementation (PR #1964)

  • Hardened PaymentSaleDeniedHandler:
    • Requires subscription resolution via binding or user_extra_data; unresolvable subscriptions are ignored with zero side-effects (no Redis write, no cc_logs_paypal poisoning).
    • Stale-event overwrite protection: compares event timestamp against existing Redis cache timestamp to prevent old failures overwriting newer active states.
    • Rate limiting: max 5 failure writes per subscription per hour before writes halt.
    • Dead-letter logging: unresolvable denied events record to Redis Toronto (paypal:needs_review:{event_id}, 30-day TTL).

2. Production E2E Verification

  • Tested SSE status stream response against Redis cached states:
    • Cache populated with failed status -> stream immediately pushed:
      {"status":"failed","is_active":false,"message":"Card declined by issuing bank","error_code":"PAYMENT_DENIED"}
    • Prevents frontend endless loading / spinner hang.
  • Verified timestamp comparison logic prevents race conditions between out-of-order COMPLETED and DENIED webhooks.

issues.display_title: Issue #1960: 🔴 [Security] PayPal webhook: remove signature-verification bypass — fail-closed verify (forged ?test_mode=1 grants free plans)
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

PayPal webhook signature verification is currently bypassed whenever isTestMode is true — and isTestMode is inferred from client-controlled inputs. This allows a forged webhook to grant any subscription plan to any user without payment.

Vulnerable code

app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Paypal/PaypalWebhookController.php:33-66

$isTestMode = str_contains($certUrl, 'sandbox')
    || (bool) env('PAYPAL_TEST_MODE', false)
    || (bool) $request->query('test_mode');   // client-controlled!

if (!$isValid) {
    if ($isTestMode) {
        Log::warning('[PaypalWebhook] Sandbox mode: bypassing signature verification failure ...');
        // falls through and PROCESSES the event
    } else {
        return response()->json(['error' => 'Invalid webhook signature'], 400);
    }
}

Attack chain

  1. Attacker POSTs POST /paypal/webhooks?test_mode=1 with a forged PAYMENT.SALE.COMPLETED payload, custom: "user_id:777|plan:agencyy", arbitrary amount.
  2. Signature check fails → bypassed because isTestMode=true → handler runs.
  3. user_id is taken from customData['user_id'] with no ownership validation (PaymentSaleCompletedHandler.php:74).
  4. processFirstPayment() → cc_purchase insert + updateUserData('agencyy', ...) → user 777 gets a premium plan without paying, plus Redis paypal:sub_status:{sid}=active.
  5. Bonus: resolveProductId() amount-fallback is also attacker-controlled (PaymentSaleCompletedHandler.php:411-426).

Important context (owner-confirmed)

  • Sandbox and live PayPal webhooks are configured to the same endpoint (one deployment, one URL). Runtime credential routing (PAYPAL_URL_TEST vs PAYPAL_URL, PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ID_TEST vs PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ID — PaypalHelper.php:46-61, PaypalWebhookHelper.php:42) must be kept.
  • paypal-cert-url header is ALSO attacker-controlled, so removing only the query param is insufficient.
  • Webhook flow now applies to all users (migration guard is obsolete) → this is acute, not theoretical.

Proposed fix (fail-closed, compatible with one-endpoint deployment)

Principle: spoofable input may route credentials, but must never gate verification.

  1. Remove $request->query('test_mode') from isTestMode inference.
  2. Remove the sandbox bypass branch entirely: verification failure → 400 always, regardless of mode.
  3. Preferred: dual-verify — attempt verification against PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ID (live), on failure retry against PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ID_TEST (sandbox); both failing → reject. The webhook id that verifies becomes isTestMode — environment is then a PayPal-attested fact instead of inferred from any spoofable input. (Fallback option: keep cert-url inference strictly for credential routing, verification stays fail-closed.)
  4. Distinguish network failure during verify (retry; existing transid idempotency makes this safe) from invalid signature (reject). Do not fail open on transient errors.
  5. Startup assertion: PAYPAL_URL must be set — paypalRequest() currently falls back to the sandbox URL by default (PaypalHelper.php:55), so a missing env would silently route live flow to sandbox.
  6. Keep PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_SKIP_VERIFY for local dev only; log CRITICAL + alert if set outside dev.

Acceptance criteria

  • No code path processes a webhook whose signature verification failed.
  • ?test_mode= query param is not referenced anywhere in isTestMode inference.
  • Sandbox webhook events still verify and process correctly (verify manually in sandbox).
  • Unit test: forged payload with test_mode=1 → 400; forged Paypal-Cert-Url: sandbox header → 400; genuine live event → 200 processed; genuine sandbox event → 200 processed.

Implementation & E2E Verification Result (2026-09-26)

1. Implementation (PR #1964, commit 1b3f4ae48 on main)

  • Implemented verifyDualEnvironment() in app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Helpers/Paypal/PaypalWebhookHelper.php:
    • Live webhook ID verified first (PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ID), fallback to test webhook ID (PAYPAL_WEBHOOK_ID_TEST).
    • Whichever webhook ID passes attests isTestMode as an authoritative PayPal fact.
  • Removed client-controllable bypass: $request->query('test_mode') eliminated.
  • Ignored spoofable paypal-cert-url header for gating verification.
  • Enforced startup assertion on PAYPAL_URL (no silent sandbox URL fallback).

2. Production E2E Verification (https://apil.gothru.co/paypal/webhooks)

  • Forged without signature headers: Returned HTTP 400 {"error":"Invalid webhook signature"}.
  • Forged with ?test_mode=1 query param: Returned HTTP 400 {"error":"Invalid webhook signature"} (bypass attempt rejected).
  • Forged with fake paypal-cert-url: sandbox header: Returned HTTP 400 {"error":"Invalid webhook signature"} (bypass attempt rejected).
  • Server log audit (lumen-2026-09-26.log on apil-1): Confirmed dual verification attempted live then test webhook ID, logged verification_status: FAILURE, and issued WARNING rejection.
  • Genuine Sandbox event (User 50214, Sub I-0SH6452H85TT): Verified with mode: sandbox, attested: true, returned HTTP 200, and processed cleanly.

issues.display_title: Issue #1967: Extend PayPal subscription status SSE stream timeout to 60s
issues.main_description_html:
Context

Subscription status SSE stream (/paypal/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/status-stream) currently times out after 45s. Extended to 60s to allow sufficient webhook processing time.

Requirements

  • Extend $maxSeconds from 45 to 60 in GetSubscriptionStatusStream.php.

Acceptance Criteria

  • SSE stream holds connection and polls up to 60s before sending status: timeout.
  • Heartbeat and data payloads remain intact.

Result Summary

  • Implementation: Set DEFAULT_MAX_SECONDS = 60 in GetSubscriptionStatusStream.php, added constructor injection and getMaxSeconds() getter for testability.
  • Testing: Passed PHPUnit unit tests (PaypalWebhookTest.php) and verified live SSE connection timeout at 60s.
  • PR: #1968
